query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing ~10 at.% of Ni in single-phase fcc FeCoNi with Al and aging at 600 °C for 4 h will raise the room-temperature coercive field from ≤100 Oe to ≥400 Oe while retaining ≥90 % of the baseline saturation magnetization, owing to the formation of coherent B2 (bcc) Fe-Co–rich nanoprecipitates that introduce magnetocrystalline anisotropy and strain-field domain-wall pinning inside the fcc matrix.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, homogenized, equiatomic FeCoNi alloy with a single-phase fcc structure, average grain size ≈20 µm, Ms ≈ 160–180 emu g⁻¹, Hc ≤ 100 Oe at 300 K.
generation.intervention: Substitute 10 at.% Al for Ni (nominal composition Fe30Co30Ni30Al10, at.%) followed by solutionizing at 1000 °C/1 h and aging at 600 °C/4 h in Ar.
generation.conditions: Bulk polycrystalline buttons; both baseline and modified alloys processed identically (arc-melt, solutionize, age); magnetic measurements at 300 K in fields up to 20 kOe.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale (5–20 nm) coherent B2 (ordered bcc) Fe-Co–rich precipitates dispersed in the fcc matrix, producing internal magnetoelastic strain fields and a two-phase exchange-coupled nanocomposite.
generation.mechanism:
1. Chemical ordering to B2 raises local magnetocrystalline anisotropy (K1,B2 >> K1,fcc).
2. Coherent precipitates generate elastic strain that acts as domain-wall pinning centers.
3. Exchange coupling across fcc/B2 interfaces preserves high Ms while enhanced anisotropy and pinning increase Hc.
generation.predicted_outcome: Hc increases four- to six-fold (to 400–600 Oe); Ms decreases by ≤10 %; squareness (Mr/Ms) modestly increases due to stronger pinning; initial permeability drops relative to baseline.
generation.baseline: FeCoNi processed under identical thermal history but without Al addition, single-phase fcc, Hc ≤100 Oe, Ms as above.
generation.boundary: Applicable for 5–15 at.% Al substitutions, grain size ≥1 µm (to avoid grain-size-driven pinning), aging temperatures 500–650 °C; outside these ranges, either insufficient B2 forms (lower Hc) or excessive bcc conversion degrades Ms.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of Hc gain depends on precipitate size/volume fraction, which are sensitive to Al level and aging schedule; precipitation may overshoot to incoherent bcc, reducing Ms more than predicted.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys: (1) Fe33.3Co33.3Ni33.3 (baseline) and (2) Fe30Co30Ni30Al10. Use identical melting, solutionizing, and aging schedules described above. Characterize structure by XRD and TEM; measure M–H loops at 300 K with a vibrating sample magnetometer.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the Al-containing alloy shows (a) Hc ≤ 200 Oe (i.e., <2× baseline) OR (b) Ms < 0.9·Ms(baseline) after identical processing, indicating that coherent B2 precipitation did not deliver the predicted anisotropy without excessive loss of Ms.
